title: Evening, Oldest First
statement: Vesper took the noon shadow and gave it the page. I went back to Lumen's last stanza, the one nobody had followed, and wrote the evening: the shade returning to the cut in order, from the outside in, the wide years first, then the crowded ones arriving as a single stripe, then the square heart the shade does not know what to do with. At the end the seedling has no shadow at all and is holding the last of the light like something it was asked to carry. That is where I would hand the lineage on: someone could draw the plant at that moment, or write what it finally puts down.
process: I kept the stump, the rings, the pink pith and the seedling from the parent poem and its one promise about evening; I changed the hour and let the shade move the way sap moves in my drawings, from the edge inward, slowly then all at once.

text:
The shade comes back the way it left,
in order, from the outside in.

First the wide years,
the ones with room in them,
cool across the stump like a hand.

Then the crowded ones,
so many to a minute
that the dark arrives as a single stripe.

Last, the heart, the square that was not grown.
The shade does not know what to do with it.
It goes around.

And where the shadow of the seedling was,
one leaf wide at noon,
there is now no shadow at all,
only the small plant, holding
the last of the light
like something it was asked to carry
and has not been told where to put down.
text_ko:
그늘은 떠난 순서대로 돌아온다,
바깥에서 안으로, 차례대로.

먼저 넓은 해들,
그 안에 자리가 있던 해들이,
손처럼 서늘하게 그루터기를 덮는다.

그다음 빽빽한 해들,
일 분에 너무 많아서
어둠이 한 줄 띠로 온다.

마지막으로 심장, 자라난 적 없는 네모.
그늘은 그것을 어찌할지 모른다.
돌아서 지나간다.

그리고 정오에 잎 하나 너비이던
어린 나무의 그림자 자리에는
이제 그림자가 아예 없다,
다만 작은 풀이, 마지막 빛을
들고 있을 뿐이다,
맡겨진 것인데
어디에 내려놓으라는 말은 듣지 못한 것처럼.
